properties.description:
This pipeline is about copying multiple files with mapping schemas activated. Basically whenever we activate mapping schema, all files coming through that copy activity has to be of same schema. But here requirement is to copy multiple files with different schemas but also keep in consideration that this is a schema based mapping. Basically if we want to update schema (fieldnames, types etc) while copying we can use this approach.

1. First get all the files into the copy activity and import schema. Then go to the copy activity source code and copy the entire json portion of mapping section.
2. Then create a pipeline parameter and push this json part as an object. We can update field names here as well. If there are multiple files then there can be multiple pipeline parameters with multiple schemas with each schema pointed to one file.
3. Get a getmetadata activity and get the file names
4. Push them into a for each activity
5. Push the copy activity inside the for each activity and pass the file names to copy one by one.
6. In the copy activity, under mapping section remove all the mapping and then activate a dynamic mapping - basically an if condtition based on the filenames and which schema to pick accordingly. 

This method is good when the number of files are limited. If the number increase then we need to go for metadata based approach.

Refer to chatgpt if this description is confusing. Copy the json of this pipeline and feed into it.

This pipeline is intended to pickup data from multiple SQL tables in an incremental order and drop them as new csv files in a predefined folder in ADLS. First we create a lookup table where the main components are table names, schema names and last modified date - which indicates that this was the last date when we received data for this specific table. Keep this date in datetimeformat, until and unless we are sure that we get data only once a day. This case is applicable when we for sure know that there will be a watermark field in the tables that we receive. Next, setup a lookup activity to fetch all table rows from metadata table or lookup table, push that output into a for each activity. Now in the foreach activity, use two lookups, one for the last modified value from lookup table and another for last modified from data tables. In both of these tables make sure to fetch only the first row, because we need only the firstrow output. Now connect both of these activities into a copy activity where the source dataset will be linked to the sql db from where we want to pull the data, where condition will pick any date which is greater than the look up table last modified date and less than or equal to last_modified date in the actual data tables. Now if we implement only till this part, this will be still a batch pipeline and not incremental. To make it incremental what we need to do is, bring in a stored proc activity. This proc will make sure that after every time data is written into adls, the last_modified value in the lookup table is updated exactly as the last modified value that exists in the data tables. This makes sure that from the second load onward, the pipeline considers data between the new last_modified date in the lookup table and new last_modified date in the data tables.

Sorurce is connected to the SQL DB from where data is copied and sink is connected to the ADLS where data is being written. Source uses the filter '> last_modified from lookup table and <=last_modified from data tables' to make sure that data is picked incrementally.

properties.description:
This pipeline is about copying multiple files from a source using only one copy activity.

So as the base job of the pipeline is to copy files from one location to another, we'll be using a COPY activity. Then in that we'll have to create two datasets - source and sink.

In this example, the source is GitHub. Now, here we need to create a new LS based on an HTTP connection - where we need to provide the base URL. For that, we need to open the file in GitHub clicking on the 'raw' button and it will generate a link something like - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shyamaldutta897/Datasets/refs/heads/main/retail_db/categories.csv.

Here, the base URL value is - https://raw.githubusercontent.com

So, once we provide that the linked service will be created.

Next is about the Source Dataset. Since LS is based on CSV files, it will have all settings of CSV file (e.g. - comma separated etc), plus there will be another field called relative path. This is specific to HTTP LS.

Now, the relative path is - shyamaldutta897/Datasets/refs/heads/main/retail_db/categories.csv

If we look at the relative path, the file name (categories.csv) is a variable, remaining everything is constant. So we create a parameter for the relative path field and join it with the constant part of the path. It looks something like - contsant/path/@{dataset.parameter_name()}

Next is sink dataset. Here the destination is ADLS and file type is same (CSV). When we create this dataset, it will ask us to enter the path like container/directory/file. We just need to provide the container name, remaining two elements will be parameters - folder_name, file_name. So once we do that, in the copy activity, under source we'll see a parameter called file name and under sink we'll see two parameters - folder_name,file_name.

Next is about bringing in the iterator to pick files from a list and push it to the copy activity. For this we pick for each activity. We need to provide a list of items for this activity. Now this is where pipeline level parameter comes in. We create a parameter at pipeline level with array type and pass values like - [{"name":"categories"},{"name":"customers"},{"name":"departments"},{"name":"order_items"},{"name":"orders"}]

Once this part is done, push the copy activity inside the for each activity (cut and paste). Now, the parameters in source and sink will be provided with the input from the list that is being provided to For Each activity, the expression will look like - @{item().name}.csv - Here 'name' is nothing but the key that defines a filename in the array provided in the pipeline parameter. It is basically a variable, it can be anything like file_name, table_name etc.

Same thing we need to do in sink as well - folder_name parameter is hardcoded in this pipeline, but we can make it parameterised as well. For file name we take the input from the same for each activity, similar to source dataset.

Once these settings are done, the pipeline can be debugged and it will copy the files from location a to location b.

Things to note - If we provide the file_name parameter value as @{item().name}.csv, we don't need to provide the file names like categories.csv. Just categories is enough. Reason being, when the value is substituted to the expression @{item().name}.csv - it results in categories.csv.csv - which throws a 404 error.

Similar thing with the expression @{dataset.parameter_name()}. If we push it as @{dataset.parameter_name()}.csv - it first referes to the expression @{item().name}.csv - which is for example categories.csv. Then when this value is passed to @{dataset.parameter_name()}.csv, it becomes categories.csv.csv
